summary: Donald Harper works in Sinology and religious studies. He taught Zhiru Shi and held posts at the University of Arizona (attested 1999) and the University of Chicago as Centennial Professor of Chinese Studies (attested 2026).

Donald K. Swearer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who taught Rory Lindsay and Thomas Adams Borchert. He held posts at Swarthmore College (~1976–2004) and Harvard University (2004–2010).

Donald Keene was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia University (~1938–1951) under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Harvard University (~1947–1948). He held academic posts at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University (1955).

Donald Phillip Verene is a philosopher who earned a bachelor's at Knox College (~1955–1959) and a doctorate at Washington University in St. Louis (~1960–1964). He served as chair at Emory University (1982–1988) and held visiting posts at Pembroke College, Oxford, and Sapienza University of Rome.

Donald R. Davis Jr. specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Richard W. Lariviere, Ludo Rocher, and Patrick Olivelle, and held faculty positions at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2012) and the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

Donald S. Lopez Jr. is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his BA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has held faculty posts at Middlebury College (1986) and the University of Michigan (from 1990).

id: P:Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso
summary: Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Dongak Chokyi Nyima was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Dongak Tendzin was a scholar who engaged in mutual study and teaching with both Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dongchu was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He served as dean at Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy (~1934–1945) and abbot at Dinghui Temple (~1945–1949).

Donna C. Kurtz is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Cincinnati (~1961–1965), Yale University (~1965–1967), and Somerville College, Oxford (~1967–1968). She held a post at the Classical Art Research Centre (~1970–2011).

Dor Bahadur Bista is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields who studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus. He served as a professor at Tribhuvan University (~1976–1990) and was a board member of the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development.

Doranne Jacobson is a scholar in Indology and other fields. She earned a doctorate in anthropology from Columbia University, where she also held a post as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

Doris Meth Srinivasan specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning degrees from Hunter College and the University of Pennsylvania, she held posts at Columbia, Barnard, George Washington University, George Mason University, the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, and Stony Brook University.
Doris Unterthurner specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Dorje Rinchen was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He studied under Sakya Yab Jé Kün Ga Rinchen, Ja Shong Lob Zur Lodrö Gyatso, Nying Ri Tri Chen Tutob Tendzin, Chime Tenpai Nyima, and Sakya Dak Chen Ngawang Kün Ga Gyaltsen.

Dorje Tseten was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied education at Beijing Normal University (~1944–1948). He later served as director of the China Tibetology Research Center from 1986 to 2000.

Dorji Banzarov was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He studied at the First Kazan Male Gymnasium and completed his doctoral dissertation at Kazan Imperial University under Józef Kowalewski (~1842–1846).

Dorji Wangchuk is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen. He has taught and held a professorship at the University of Hamburg since 1998.

Dorothy C. Wong works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She has held posts as a visiting professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009) and as affiliate faculty at the University of Virginia (attested 2026).
